answer: Conductance-cut detection resists sybils: a fake cluster has dense internal attestations but few edges crossing to the honest core, giving low conductance, the ratio of boundary edges to internal volume. The system finds sparse cuts and discounts any region sitting like an island behind a thin canyon of forgeable attack edges. Adding more clones inside only raises internal volume without widening that fixed boundary, so the cluster's trust signal only shrinks per fake. Honest nodes, woven by many crossing edges, keep high conductance and full weight.
